newsitem.title: USA: Arthuis says Italy's budget efforts encouraging.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis says Italy's budget efforts encouraging.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said on Monday Italy's efforts to cut its budget deficit were encouraging, but made no comment on whether he thought they would be enough to let Rome qualify for European monetary union in 1999.
"Italy is taking this initiative. One has to let Italy put it into practice," he told a news conference at the annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

"I find it very encouraging," he said, adding that he welcomed the fact that all countries were taking action to meet Maastricht treaty criteria in 1997, the crucial year for deciding which countries qualify for monetary union in 1999.
"There is a powerful and irreversible movement towards the single currency," he said.
Italian Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco said in Rome on Monday that some of Italy's European partners wanted to keep Italy out of a single currency, but declined to name them.
